tool: EasyMultiProfiler (EMP) — R workflow for microbiome multi-omics integration
strengths: Standardized five-module pipeline using SummarizedExperiment/MultiAssayExperiment classes for host-microbiome integration with reproducibility focus.
limitations: Microbiome-focused scope; R/SummarizedExperiment workflow requires programming expertise and dedicated infrastructure.

strengths: Captures shared and modality-specific variation through latent factors; supports subtyping, imputation and outlier detection.
limitations: Unsupervised factors are biologically hard to interpret; primarily validated on bulk data with specific generative assumptions.

tool: mixOmics — R package for multivariate 'omics integration
strengths: Mature R package with PLS-based methods for dimension reduction and feature selection across multiple 'omics types.
limitations: Mostly pairwise PLS-based integration; less suited for very large or single-cell multi-omics datasets.

tool: MOFA+ — statistical framework for single-cell multi-modal integration (Python/R)
strengths: Scalable variational inference with flexible sparsity priors; jointly models multi-modal single-cell data across samples.
limitations: Requires multi-modal single-cell data; factor interpretation remains challenging and computationally intensive at scale.

tool: Similarity Network Fusion (SNF) — R/Matlab network fusion for sample integration
strengths: Fuses per-data-type similarity networks into a unified network; effective for cancer subtyping and survival prediction.
limitations: Sensitive to similarity metric and hyperparameters; designed for sample-level rather than feature-level integration.

tool: MUUMI — R package for statistical meta-analysis and network-based multi-omics integration
strengths: Unifies single-omics meta-analysis with network-based multi-omics integration, including SNF, to find robust signatures.
limitations: Recently released; demonstrated primarily on IPF and macrophage datasets, so broader validation is still pending.

tool: moiraine — R package for reproducible multi-omics integration pipelines
strengths: Automates preprocessing, formatting, visualization and side-by-side comparison of multiple integration tools.
limitations: Pipeline orchestrator rather than a new integration method; depends on third-party tools for actual analysis.

tool: BioNeuralNet — Python framework for GNN-based multi-omics network analysis
strengths: Modular framework interoperable with PyTorch/scikit-learn/NetworkX; supports end-to-end network-based multi-omics workflows.
limitations: Requires user-built networks; GNN training is data-hungry and outputs depend heavily on network quality.

tool: Profiler — open-source web/desktop platform for multi-omics analysis
strengths: Unified QC, preprocessing, statistics, ML/DL, biomarker and survival analyses across multiple omics types.
limitations: Web/desktop architecture may limit scalability; breadth of features can sacrifice depth versus specialized tools.

tool: SUMO — R package for simulating multi-omics datasets
strengths: Generates factor-analysis-based multi-omics data with user-controlled latent structure, shared/distinct factors and noise.
limitations: Simulation-only utility; synthetic structure may not fully capture real-world data heterogeneity and batch effects.

tool: single-cell analyst — web platform for single-cell multi-omics
strengths: Supports six single-cell modalities plus spatial transcriptomics with automated QC, processing and many interactive visualizations.
limitations: GUI-driven workflow limits custom analyses; primarily single-cell focused with less bulk multi-omics flexibility.

tool: Analyst software suite — web-based multi-omics integration (ExpressAnalyst, MetaboAnalyst, OmicsNet, OmicsAnalyst)
strengths: Combines single-omics, knowledge-driven network integration and data-driven dimensionality reduction with documented protocols.
limitations: Each component handles separate omics types; cross-component workflows can be fragmented with upload size limits.
